messages:
auditor_jane: Hi team, auditor here — we need evidence that key rotation for the production KMS key preserves access to historical audit data and that rotation events are logged. Can you show the control mapping to SOC 2 and what artifacts we can export?

maria: Hey @auditor_jane — short answer: yes, rotation is performed as envelope-key rotation so existing ciphertext remains decryptable with older key material. We map this to the 'logical access & change management' control in our SOC 2 pack.

aj: Adding details — we store data encrypted with a per-object data key (DEK) that is envelope-encrypted with the KMS key (KEK). When a KEK rotates, DEKs remain unchanged; KMS retains previous key versions for decryption.

sam: For artifacts we can provide: CloudTrail/KMS API event export (CreateKey, ScheduleKeyDeletion, RotateKey, DisableKey), KMS key version list, signed manifest of rotation events, and sample decryption verification logs.

secops_bot: [automated] Export prepared: s3://compliance-exports/4950012345/kms-rotation-manifest.tar.gz (ready in ~10m) :package: 

auditor_jane: Thanks. For the KMS events, can you show exact commands you used to create the export and a minimal sample of the event format? Auditor wants reproducible steps.

maria: Sure — AWS example steps we used (we're multi-cloud but auditor asked for AWS sample):
```bash
aws cloudtrail lookup-events --lookup-attributes AttributeKey=EventSource,AttributeValue=kms.amazonaws.com 
  --start-time 2025-01-01T00:00:00Z --end-time 2025-12-31T23:59:59Z 
  --query 'Events[?contains(Resources[0].ResourceName, `alias/rdw-prod-kms`)]' > kms-events.json
aws kms list-keys --query 'Keys[].KeyId' > keyids.json
for id in $(cat keyids.json); do aws kms describe-key --key-id $id >> keys-describe.json; done
```
Sample event (trimmed):
```json
{
  "EventId": "e-abc123",
  "EventName": "ScheduleKeyDeletion",
  "EventTime": "2025-07-12T18:23:11Z",
  "Resources": [{"ResourceType":"AWS::KMS::Key","ResourceName":"alias/rdw-prod-kms"}],
  "Username": "kms-admin@redwood.com"
}
```

aj: We also ran a decryption verification for a random sample of archived blobs: process was `decrypt-with-kms --key-alias alias/rdw-prod-kms --ciphertext sample_blob.bin` which logs successful decrypt and key version used. We can include the verification output (hash of plaintext + keyVersion id) in the evidence bundle.

auditor_jane: Good. Two follow-ups: 1) How do you prove chain-of-custody for those exported logs (signed, tamper-evident)? 2) Are there any edge cases where a rotation could break historical decryption (e.g., manual re-encryption, external key policies)?

maria: 1) Chain-of-custody: we sign the exported tarball with our compliance GPG key and upload to S3 with MFA-delete enabled and object-lock in governance mode. The manifest includes SHA256 checksums for each file and a signed statement with who exported it and the job id. 2) Edge cases: the only risk is if someone manually re-encrypts data with a different KEK or rewraps DEKs. We detect rewraps via CloudTrail events (ReEncrypt) and by validating DEK key IDs stored in metadata; any mismatch triggers an alert.

sam: Also note our rotation policy: automatic rotation every 90 days for customer-facing KEKs, retention of all prior key versions for 7 years to satisfy forensic needs. We document the rotation schedule in the key metadata and include the rotation ARN in evidence.

auditor_jane: OK please attach the following in the bundle: (A) kms-events.json (filtered), (B) keys-describe.json, (C) sample decrypt verification outputs with hashes, (D) signed manifest, (E) policy screenshots for alias/rdw-prod-kms. Can you confirm ETA?

secops_bot: [automated] export job started: job_id=job-20250315-22 ; estimated completion 12 minutes.

maria: ETA ~20 minutes — secops_bot is packaging and we will run the signed manifest step once bundle is ready. Will ping here with S3 path + signature.

aj: I'll also prepare a short mapping doc showing which fields in those artifacts map to SOC 2 criteria (access controls, change logs, evidence of monitoring). I'll drop it to the bundle as `control_mapping.md`.

auditor_jane: Great. One last ask — include a small sampled timeline that ties a key rotation event to an example incident investigation (how you would decrypt archived blobs and link to CloudTrail entries). A 4–5 step narrative is fine.

maria: Will do — example timeline will be included. :thumbsup:

sam: Marking action items: export complete -> sign -> upload -> post link here. I'll run a final sanity check on the DEK metadata after export.

auditor_jane: Thanks all — will review bundle when posted."
